title: Downtown Memory Loop
summary: A short loop from the station to the theater, the park, and the museum campus: how a railroad stop became a town, and what it does after dark.

topic.name: Rail and the Commuter Town
topic.description: How the Chicago, Burlington & Quincy line turned a farm settlement into a railroad suburb, and how the daily commute still shapes downtown.

place.name: Main Street Station
place.summary: The downtown commuter rail stop on the BNSF line, successor to the Chicago, Burlington & Quincy depot that put Downers Grove on the map.

featured_moment.title: The Burlington Arrives
featured_moment.excerpt: In 1864 the Chicago, Burlington & Quincy Railroad laid its line through the settlement that Pierce Downer had founded three decades earlier. The tracks did what the farm never could: they made it possible to live here and work in Chicago.…

stops.note: Start where the town started: the tracks.

place.name: Tivoli Theatre
place.summary: A 1928 movie palace built for sound films, still running first-run pictures under its original marquee.

featured_moment.title: Built for the Talkies
featured_moment.excerpt: The Tivoli opened on Christmas Day 1928 as one of the first theaters in the country designed from the start for sound films, arriving only a year after "The Jazz Singer" proved that audiences wanted to hear the movies. Its Renaissance…

stops.note: The railroad brought people; the theater gave them a reason to stay downtown.

place.name: Fishel Park
place.summary: A small downtown park with a bandshell, home of the summer concert series and a century of village gatherings.
place.address: Grove St & Curtiss St, Downers Grove, IL

featured_moment.title: Summer Concert Lawn
featured_moment.excerpt: Fishel Park is small enough to cross in a minute and large enough to hold the village on a summer evening. The bandshell hosts the park district's free summer concert series, and the lawn fills with folding chairs, blankets, and children…

stops.note: A breather on the lawn before the longer leg north.

place.name: Downers Grove Museum
place.summary: The village history campus, anchored by the 1846 Blodgett House and run by the park district.

featured_moment.title: The Blodgett House
featured_moment.excerpt: Israel Blodgett, a blacksmith, built this house in 1846, a generation before the railroad. It is one of the oldest surviving buildings in the village, and family tradition holds that the Blodgetts sheltered freedom seekers on the…

stops.note: End a generation before the railroad, in the blacksmith's house.
